speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand what is causing your acute diarrhea. How long have you had these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or pus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). The history of recent levofloxacin use combined with acute watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. Please confirm if you have experienced fever or if your stool has been particularly foul-smelling.
